description: M5 item 7 — installer VirtIO target. Same transactional installer self-test as item 6 (tools/m6_installer_markers.json) but the blank scratch disk is attached on the VirtIO bus (legacy virtio-blk-pci -> vd0) instead of AHCI, proving the installer and its block I/O work over VirtIO as well as AHCI. The kernel's virtio_blk driver now honours multi-sector block buffers (vd0_read/vd0_write loop per sector), so gpt::write, dunitfs::format, the ESP copy, verify and install_bios all run through the generic block registry against vd0. find_scratch_target()/plan() accept driver in {ahci, virtio-blk}. On an ISO boot the AHCI controller is present but carries no data disk (the CD is ATAPI), so the only writable scratch target is vd0. Run (BIOS): tools/qemu_test.py --build --markers-file tools/m7_installer_virtio_markers.json --timeout 420 --boot-timeout 380 --post-boot-delay 2 --settle 2 --require-marker '[BOOT] firmware=BIOS'. Run (UEFI): add --uefi and --require-marker '[BOOT] firmware=UEFI'.

required.claim: the virtio-blk scratch disk came up as a writable block device
the installer self-test launched before auto_mount
the installer selected the VirtIO disk as its target
rollback restored both partition-table snapshots on VirtIO after the injected fault
the VirtIO scratch's FRONT/BACK regions are byte-identical to the pre-write state and no GPT remains — rollback is real over VirtIO
the clean transaction ran all phases to a commit over VirtIO
the VirtIO-installed disk reads back with ESP + DUNIT-SYSTEM, a Clean fsck, and a bootable MBR signature
both installer self-test phases passed over VirtIO
the freshly installed VirtIO DUNIT-SYSTEM partition was mounted at /persist by auto_mount — the install is real and mountable
the Live system booted to the terminal after all self-tests

forbidden.why: the VirtIO scratch disk was not detected as an install target
the installer self-test failed over VirtIO
rollback did not restore the partition table on VirtIO
the clean VirtIO install did not read back consistent
the rollback write-back itself failed on VirtIO
